title: Chelsea: Palmer's Slump, a Red Card and a Leaking Defence
body:
Chelsea's Cole Palmer is back in the spotlight, with BBC Sport asking whether the player from his 2024 form can return [S1]. The question is tied to the side's wider slump, which has seen results drift as the season goes on [S1].

The frustration is the telling detail. It was evident after the defeat against Leeds [S1]. A separate BBC Sport explainer has also covered his red card suspension, which it says will not rule him out of the Premier League match against Manchester United [S2]. Two stories about one player, and they point in different directions.

The numbers back up the mood. Chelsea's last five league games read WLWLL: two wins, three defeats, six points, five scored and seven conceded [ST1]. Leeds United, over their last five, have collected eight points from DDLWW, with six scored and four conceded [ST2]. Those figures show a side that is giving away too much at both ends.

The suspension is the smaller problem. The bigger one is a team that cannot protect a lead or close out a game, and a manager who needs answers on the pitch rather than in press conferences.

The Touchline Take: one to keep an eye on.

evidence.text: BBC Sport: Will 2024 version of Palmer ever re-emerge for Chelsea?. Cole Palmer's dip in form mirrors Chelsea's recent slump and his frustration was evident after his side's recent defeat against Leeds - but will he ever get back to his best?
